E.1.1. Overview
#
PostgreSQL
19 contains many new features and enhancements, including:
New
REPACK
command that reclaims disk space and reorganizes table contents, which can improve query performance.
REPACK (CONCURRENTLY)
allows repacking without blocking reads and writes to the table.
pg_plan_advice
extension for controlling query planner decisions and
pg_stash_advice
extension that applies plan advice automatically based on the query.
Better performance in many areas, including automatic scaling of the number of I/O worker processes, quicker foreign-key checks, and further planning and execution optimizations.
Logical replication can now be enabled without a server restart when
wal_level
is set to
replica .
Logical replication of
sequence values .
Support for
“ read-your-writes ”
consistency on standbys via the new
WAIT
command.
Parallel autovacuum of table indexes
and
autovacuum prioritization
through a new scoring system.

If you build a coding helper, you'll soon want the model to point at exact lines: "the bug is on line 212", "replace lines 40 to 52". The usual trick is to number every line before you paste the file into the prompt. It works, and it's cheap to write: one
enumerate
call.
It isn't cheap to send. I measured it, and in the most common format the numbers add 42% to the tokens of the code.
A few words first
A
token
is a chunk of text the model reads; APIs bill per million of them. A
tokenizer
is the program that cuts text into tokens; I used tiktoken with
o200k_base , the one OpenAI's current models use.
Input
tokens are everything you send in the request, priced at the input rate. A
list price
is the vendor's official price per million tokens, before any discount.
cat -n
is the Unix command that prints a file with line numbers; many tools copy its layout: the number padded to six characters, then a tab.

final_briefs.title: PostgreSQL 19
final_briefs.description: **PostgreSQL 19 adds powerful new maintenance and performance features.** Highlights include the REPACK command (with a CONCURRENTLY option) for reclaiming disk space without blocking reads/writes, planner‑advice extensions pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice, automatic scaling of I/O workers, faster foreign‑key checks, logical replication that can be enabled without a restart, read‑your‑writes consistency via the WAIT command, and parallel autovacuum of indexes with a new scoring system. The release date is 2026‑11‑19, and migration requires a dump/restore, pg_upgrade, or logical replication.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: These additions cut downtime, improve query performance, and make large‑scale PostgreSQL deployments easier to manage and scale.
final_briefs.who_cares: Backend engineers, database administrators, and data platform teams that run PostgreSQL in production.

final_briefs.title: Line numbers made the code I send to an LLM 42% more expensive
final_briefs.description: **Adding line numbers to code snippets inflates LLM token usage by roughly 42 %.** A measurement on the Python 3.13 standard library (131 files, 107 041 lines) showed that the typical `cat -n` format (seven‑digit number, tab, code) increased tokens from 893 573 to 1 272 868, a +42.4 % rise. Since LLM APIs charge per token, this overhead can noticeably raise costs for coding assistants that prepend line numbers for reference.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Prompt engineers and AI‑powered coding tool developers need to redesign how they reference code to avoid unnecessary token bloat and keep API bills under control.
final_briefs.who_cares: AI‑powered coding tool developers, prompt engineers, and anyone optimizing LLM usage budgets.
